Origin of Computers

Alan Turing effectively invented the modern day computer in a paper he submitted to the London Mathematical Society in the summer of 1936. He was not the first person to come up with the idea — that honor probably goes to Charles Babbage — but he was the first to fully understand its power. When we talk about computers today we mean
machines, but it is worth noting computers in Turing's time were more often humans using pencil and paper. The mechanical computers before

Turing were elementary at best.
